prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the very near person from the surrounding concrete enclosure: in frames 1–2 the person fills the upper-centre/right foreground and appears roughly 0.2–0.6 m from the camera, while the walls and floor extend about 0.5–3 m away around and behind them. It also reveals the enclosure's sloping surfaces and corners more clearly than RGB, including nearer lower surfaces and more distant upper/side recesses, although exact scale and the distinction between wall and floor remain uncertain. Across frames 2–4 the near person moves out of the main view as the camera turns or shifts, leaving mostly the enclosure; a small body part or shoe remains at the lower edge in frames 3–4, within roughly 0.3–0.8 m. In frame 5 another partial person appears at the upper-right edge, about 0.3–1 m away and partly occluded by the image boundary; broad smooth gradients, black holes near borders, and inconsistent values on bright openings make the map unreliable for precise distances or person-to-person spacing.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates people from the otherwise unlabeled enclosure, making their silhouettes and heavy cropping clearer than in RGB. Frames 1–2 contain a large person mask spanning the upper foreground and extending to the bottom, consistent with someone about 0.2–0.6 m away and partly surrounding or crossing the camera's forward view; the apparent split into two person instances is likely unreliable because the RGB suggests overlapping or contiguous clothing/body regions. A tiny pink fragment at the bottom of frame 2 or 3 indicates another partly visible body region within roughly arm's reach, while frame 5 contains a separate partial person at the upper-right boundary, perhaps 0.3–1 m from the wearer and several metres in scene position from the earlier foreground person, though their mutual distance cannot be recovered reliably from this map alone. The masks show left/right occupancy and occlusion over time, but they provide no labels for the concrete surfaces, cannot establish facing or gaze direction, and miss or fragment several visible shoes and limbs.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black in all five frames, so it supports no reliable body, hand, facing, gaze, reach, or inter-person spatial inference. In RGB, people or body parts are visible very close to the camera in frames 1–2, near the lower edge in frames 3–4, and partly at the upper-right in frame 5, but none receives a yellow body skeleton or magenta hand skeleton. Consequently, the map cannot clarify joint locations, whether anyone faces the wearer, which limbs are above or below others, or whether hands are within arm's reach. Its failure is likely associated with extreme proximity, severe cropping, occlusion, unusual viewpoint, and limited visible anatomy, so the absence of skeletons should not be interpreted as an absence of people.
